A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VeriTaS benchmark. All 27 pages of v1 and 35 pages of v2, including their appendices, tables, figures, and scoring definitions, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark statistics, human annotation validation, Q4 2025 model evaluations, and longitudinal performance analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original Q1 2026 evaluations, expanded human validation, and new shortcut, duplication, and pipeline-backbone sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix A explicitly reports upgrading pipeline components from Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash to Gemini 3.1 Pro/3 Flash for Q1 2026. The seven-stage construction procedure, ensemble aggregation, integrity rule, and rectification approach remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Coverage extends through Q1 2026, adding newly emerging claims for post-cutoff evaluation. The benchmark retains its open-domain fact-checking task, text/image/video coverage, and 54 languages; the reported source mix changes from 108 to 104 fact-checking organizations.

E2.justification: The main comparisons replace older Gemini baselines and add Claude Opus 4.6, Gemma 4, and Qwen 3.5. DEFAME and LOKI change from GPT-5.2 backbones to three other backbones each. Their longitudinal result rows in v1 Table 8 are absent from v2 Table 9.

E3.justification: V2 adds seven-bin accuracy, speech transcripts alongside sampled video frames, and a screened Prolific annotation phase, expanding evaluated integrity claims from 63 to 204. The longitudinal sample grows from 2,400 to 2,500. Appendix J.1 retains temporal search filtering but no longer specifies v1's fact-checker-domain blacklist, leaving its continued use unresolved.

E4.justification: V2 expands single-model annotation ablations and adds original-versus-rectified claim comparisons, duplicate analysis, and regeneration of 689 claims with alternative pipeline backbones (Appendices F–H). It also adds language/integrity breakdowns, baseline confusion matrices, and detailed analysis of human–model disagreements.

E5.justification: Both versions report single-run benchmarking without confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-based uncertainty estimates. Larger human-validation samples and additional confidence-label accuracy results do not introduce a new statistical uncertainty reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V1 Table 4 reports Gemini 3 Pro as best by MSE on Q4 2025, reaching 0.39 with search; v2 Table 3 reports Claude Opus 4.6 at 0.183 on Q1 2026 under revised settings. Human integrity accuracy changes from 96.8% to 97.5% on an expanded sample. Numerous new subset, ablation, and sensitivity results are reported.

T1.justification: Appendix C and Figure 6 add an explicit continuous-score-to-seven-bin mapping for the newly reported seven-bin accuracy. V1 listed seven prediction values but specified accuracy using three bins. The integrity definition, ensemble arithmetic, and MSE interpretation remain unchanged; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a first dynamic multimodal AFC benchmark, automated quarterly construction, disentangled uncertainty-aware annotations, human agreement, and evidence that pre-cutoff evaluation overestimates capability. Updated dataset counts and supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretation of rectified-claim realism, proprietary-backbone dependence, duplication, and stylistic shortcuts. Appendix K.3 explains authenticity ambiguities and cross-property errors. Discussion also revises the interpretation of open-model competitiveness and adds limitations concerning ambiguous claims, satire, and evaluation of evidence quality.

D1.justification: V1 promises code/data release; v2 reports availability and introduces a Claim Browser exposing 104,000 gathered claims, including dismissed ones, with researcher-gated access. V2 also documents additional filtering and sampling details, updated model versions, scrapeMM tooling, annotation tutorial links, and revised construction costs.

R1.justification: The reference lists and related-benchmark comparison are substantively unchanged. Updating XFacta's stated time since its last update from five to eight months preserves the same research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes local language corrections, expands scoring and metric explanations, rewrites parts of the Discussion, and reorganizes the appendices. The main section sequence and most introductory and methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are refreshed or redrawn, and v1's compact statistics table becomes v2's substantial Figure 4 infographic. The principal results table gains grouped subset columns. New discretization diagrams, analysis tables, distribution plots, confusion matrices, and browser screenshots substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the automated benchmark: human evaluation expands from 63 to 204 integrity claims, while new shortcut, duplication, backbone-sensitivity, and disagreement analyses address previously untested validity concerns. The Q1 2026 extension demonstrates updating, and reported code/data access improves auditability. Stale appendix counts, conflicting smoothing-window labels, and unclear blacklist documentation remain, but these reporting issues do not outweigh the stronger validation and reproducibility.
